2.2

Seeing the ordinary

Apply painting conventions

Use drawing methods to apply knowledge of conventions appropriate to painting

Suggested teaching time
4 weeks

Timing, task steps and quantities are classroom suggestions, not NZQA grade requirements.

Read the standard (PDF)

The brief

How can viewpoint, colour and paint surface transform familiar objects?

Use drawing as practical investigation to apply painting conventions to an arrangement of your own objects. Build knowledge by making: drawing includes painted studies, colour studies and collage as well as pencil work. Focus on choosing methods for a particular visual purpose.

Materials & preparation

Objects, sketchbook, drawing media, collage paper made from your own marks, acrylic or gouache, prepared study supports and a limited set of brushes.

Use your own drawings and photographs as starting points. Record sources and seek permission for people, places and culturally significant material. Discuss tikanga and context with your teacher where relevant.

Artist connections

Choose the connections that serve your intention. The contemporary models offer different approaches; select a relevant comparison rather than studying every artist. These works are references, not assessment exemplars.

Compare flat colour, compressed figure relationships and densely organised garden space. Select conventions for a particular pictorial purpose in your own observed subject.

  • Ayesha Green

    Contemporary Māori · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Green’s flattened colour and still-life subjects open questions about representation, whenua and national identity. Read the context before comparing how an object can carry a public story and a personal association.

    McCahon House · Still Life education resource (PDF) · Painting investigation

  • Kushana Bush

    Contemporary · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Bush’s gouache paintings organise figures, gestures and intricate detail within a flattened picture plane. Investigate how relationships between people and the repetition of forms can suggest a narrative.

    QAGOMA · artist profile and collection · Painting investigation

  • Jadé Fadojutimi

    Contemporary · United Kingdom

    Look closely at the colour relationships, layered marks and shifting forms in Fadojutimi’s paintings, then watch Tate’s studio film. Consider how everyday experiences and personal interests can become starting points for abstract painting.

    Artist’s official website · paintings · Painting investigation

  • Paul Cézanne

    France

    Study the tilted table, overlapping forms and repeated touches of colour in The Basket of Apples. Investigate how a stable object can sit inside an unsettled picture space.

    Artist resource

Studio sequence

Use this as a flexible route through the learning. Let the work suggest the next move.

  1. Observe a changing arrangement

    Set up a small still life from objects you can draw directly. Record different viewpoints and overlaps. Identify a pictorial purpose, such as making the arrangement feel unstable, intimate or monumental.

  2. Identify usable conventions

    Investigate two artist models. Identify particular spatial, colour and surface conventions, then test their effects with your own arrangement. Label the source and the convention, not just the artist’s name.

  3. Make comparative drawing studies

    Keep the subject related while changing a deliberate variable: compressed depth versus open depth, warm versus cool modelling, or thin versus opaque paint. Compare the pictorial consequences.

  4. Select for a purpose

    Choose the methods best suited to your intention. Develop more sustained painted drawings that apply those choices together. Where a method fights your purpose, revise or reject it.

  5. Review the application

    Lay out the studies so your selection and use of conventions are visible. Explain one successful technical decision and one change. The practical work should demonstrate the knowledge without relying on a long essay.

A useful studio conversation

Put two related works side by side. Describe what changed, show the evidence and explain what you will investigate next. Invite feedback, then make your own decision.

Presentation & submission

Your teacher will confirm the assessment window, support available, final evidence and local authenticity procedures. This sheet is an original teaching resource; it is not an NZQA-issued assessment. Compare NZQA’s annotated exemplars.

What changes between grades?

Student-friendly guidance adapted from the standard. The whole body of relevant evidence determines the grade; the examples below illustrate possibilities.

Grade distinctions for AS91311
GradeWhat the evidence needs to show
AchievementApply relevant painting processes and pictorial conventions in practical work.In this task: Studies use colour, space or surface conventions appropriately.
MeritSelect and apply particular conventions for an intended purpose.In this task: A chosen palette and spatial structure directly support the intended atmosphere.
ExcellenceMake critical selections and apply an in-depth knowledge of conventions.In this task: You compare alternatives and combine appropriate methods convincingly for the intended effect.

Authority: NZQA AS91311 achievement criteria and explanatory notes (PDF).

Watch for

Copying an artist image can conceal whether you can select conventions for your own purpose.

Pause & reflect

Choose two studies. Why is one combination of methods better suited to your intention? Explain using visible features.

These optional working notes belong to you. This website does not submit assessment evidence.

Teacher notes

Planning, assessment & differentiation

Assess applied knowledge in the drawings, not the quantity of research writing. Confirm local conditions and authenticity procedures, and moderate against the 91311 exemplars. The focus is the selection and application of conventions; a separate series-development task belongs to 2.3.

Support and stretch

For teaching practice, reduce the number of simultaneous choices, model one material process and invite oral discussion alongside drawing. Offer vocabulary prompts and accessible media. To extend the learning, ask students to compare alternatives, justify a rejection or investigate a consequence of their own decision. Adapt assessed support to the standard’s conditions and any approved arrangements.

Before issuing the task

Set local start and finish dates, agree available materials and check the current standard, conditions and exemplars. Use school authenticity processes and your normal moderation procedures. Adjust this brief to the class and context; it has not been quality assured by NZQA.
